q1.title: What capability is being added or changed?
q1.imperative: Frame the mission in behavior terms: sunset the teaching half of skills/workbench (SKILL.md, references/checklist-engine.md, references/status-model.md) since the MCP door's tool schemas now teach the engine mechanism directly; keep the four templates at their current path; deregister workbench as an actively-taught skill without moving templates or requiring new installer mechanism where avoidable. Plus fix #561 (CREW_CONTEXT.md's Python Invocation section, measured wrong on this host).
q1.finding: Capability confirmed against LAUNCH_ORDER Mission + Pre-Rulings: delete workbench's teaching half where genuinely redundant with the door, keep all 4 templates at skills/workbench/templates/ unmoved, deregister workbench from being taught as a procedure, and fix #561.

q2.title: Does the door's tool schema carry what checklist-engine.md and status-model.md teach, in full?
q2.imperative: Resolve by reading both docs and the 12 MCP door tool schemas (spine_status/spine_lease/spine_start/spine_advance/spine_evidence/spine_halt/spine_survey_result/spine_capture/spine_amend/spine_bind/spine_close/spine_open). Compare content section by section.
q2.finding: PARTIAL, not full: door tool schemas carry verb loop, evidence shape (attest/attach/waive incl. override_policy), ordering, session-lease claim/heartbeat/release incl. force+reason, rework/reopen cascade, survey-vs-gated split (implied by separate tools), bubble-up (flag-candidate/block). NOT carried: (1) tests/test_mcp_adoption.py Tier2/Tier3 hard-pin two files -- skills/workbench/SKILL.md's 'Checklist engine' paragraph and checklist-engine.md's '## MCP door' + '## Session lease' sections -- as the sole written authority that the door is the DEFAULT while the CLI (checklist_engine.py) remains available, incl. a byte-exact sentence 'Nothing here removes or discourages the CLI.' and the dispatched-subagent-uses-CLI-for-its-own-plan rule (MCP scope). (2) tests/test_install_constellation.py:344-352 asserts checklist-engine.md exists post-install with its <skill-dir> token substituted for the real checklist_engine.py path. Deleting these sections/files outright breaks 2 independent, pre-existing test suites that assert this exact content is the corpus's sole documented authority for door-vs-CLI coexistence -- this is a genuine gap, not carried by tool schemas, and not safe to silently delete.

q3.title: Is deregistering workbench while keeping templates in place a state install_constellation.py already supports?
q3.imperative: Read scripts/install_constellation.py's discover_skills() and SKILL_REFERENCE_BUNDLES/SKILL_SCRIPT_BUNDLES/HOOK_OWNER_SKILL. Determine whether a skills/workbench/ directory with a template-only body but no teaching content is installable without new installer code.
q3.finding: NOT supported today. install_constellation.py:317-324 discover_skills() requires EVERY non-underscore-prefixed dir under skills/ to have a parseable SKILL.md with name+description frontmatter, or it raises InstallError for the WHOLE installer (not scoped to workbench). skills/_shared/ is the only skip (underscore prefix), and 'workbench-stays-a-template-package' + the Admiral's ruling explicitly reject renaming/moving the directory (would churn every skills/workbench/templates/X path reference, incl. the Admiral spine's own execute precondition). A zero-content or missing SKILL.md at skills/workbench/ is therefore not installable without new installer code (teaching a directory-specific exemption from the SKILL.md requirement). A minimal-but-present SKILL.md is the only supported path today.

q4.title: How should workbench be deregistered, given the installer constraint found at q3?
q4.imperative: This is 'How workbench is deregistered -- yours' per Inherited Latitude. Decide and record the chosen mechanism, citing the launch order's grant of latitude.
q4.finding: Decision: keep SKILL.md, checklist-engine.md, status-model.md present (satisfies discover_skills()) but shrink each to the minimum content that is either (a) genuinely load-bearing per q3/q2's measured findings, or (b) structurally required frontmatter. Delete everything else. SKILL.md becomes a short retired/template-only notice plus the one Tier2-pinned 'Checklist engine' default-path paragraph. checklist-engine.md keeps only its opening CLI-invocation sentence, '## MCP door', and '## Session lease' sections; deletes TOC + 9 other sections the door's schemas or self-describing gate text already carry. status-model.md keeps only 'Crew Return Status' (cited by tests/test_commander_evidence_convention.py and skills/commander/templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md:106); deletes Gate Status/Review Verdict/Commander Gate Decision as door-observable or non-mechanism prose. No new installer mechanism needed. Floating the alternative (a first-class 'retired skill' installer state) to the Admiral as a cleaner long-term fix, not built here.

q5.title: Is CREW_CONTEXT.md's Python Invocation section (#561) actually wrong on this host, and how should it be corrected?
q5.imperative: Measure which python/py/python3 have pytest installed on this Linux host and compare against the doc's 2026-08-10 claim.
q5.finding: Confirmed wrong on this host as of 2026-08-17. Measured: py, python, and python3 ALL resolve to Python 3.12.3 with pytest 9.1.1 installed ('which py python python3' -> /home/tommy/.local/bin/py, /home/tommy/.local/bin/python, /usr/bin/python3; all three 'X -m pytest --version' succeed). CREW_CONTEXT.md's 2026-08-10 claim that python3 resolves to /usr/bin/python3.12 'but has no pytest installed' no longer holds -- pytest is now installed for python3 too. Fix: update the measured claim to reflect all three now having pytest, re-affirm the check-before-you-run instruction stands regardless (a future host or python3 reinstall could diverge again), and refresh the measurement date/host note.
